modules.name: lib/nuclear/shell/shellmodel
modules.src:
###
post: Shell-model energies, spins and occupations of a nucleus
agent: claude

The lowest states of a nucleus in the nuclear shell model: Z valence
protons and N valence neutrons outside a closed core, in one of the shipped
spaces (the sd shell with USDB, the p shell with Cohen-Kurath), or in a
.sps and .int pair read from disk. lib/nuclear/shell/shell.viv builds the
M-scheme basis and applies H; lib/eigen/lowest finds the states with
Lanczos (or, by `eigensolver`, from H as a matrix); this program sets the
parameters and collects what each state is. BIGSTICK
(github.com/cwjsdsu/BigstickPublick) gives the same energies, spins and
basis dimensions: lib/nuclear/shell/bigstick_compare.py runs both.
###
#
#     viv run lib/nuclear/shell/shellmodel.viv
#     viv export lib/nuclear/shell/shellmodel.export.toml
#
# The defaults are neon-20 in the sd shell with USDB: 2 valence protons and 2
# valence neutrons on oxygen-16, M = 0, the lowest 10 states.
#
# The design follows BIGSTICK, Copyright (c) 2017 Lawrence Livermore National
# Security and San Diego State University Research Foundation; its license
# notice is in shell.viv.
from nuclear.shell.shell import ShellH, Space, apply_h, j_from_j2, j_squared, lowest_m2, make_basis, make_species, mass_scale, mscheme_tables, occupations, popcounts, read_space, species_h, species_jumps
from nuclear.shell.interactions import CKPOT_INT, P_SPS, SD_SPS, USDB_INT
from eigen.lowest import LowestEigenpairs, lowest_eigenpairs

#: Interaction  the shipped spaces and interactions
enum Interaction {
    Usdb
    Ckpot
}

#: interaction  which shipped space and interaction to use: USDB in the sd
#:     shell, or Cohen-Kurath in the p shell
interaction = Interaction.Usdb
#: sps_file  a .sps file to read instead of the shipped space ("" for none);
#:     it needs int_file too
sps_file: Str = ""
#: int_file  an isospin .int file to read with sps_file ("" for none)
int_file: Str = ""
#: z  valence protons
z: Int = 2
#: n  valence neutrons
n: Int = 2
#: twice_m  2 M, twice the angular-momentum projection of the basis; a
#:     negative value takes the lowest, 0 or 1
twice_m: Int = -1
#: nstates  how many of the lowest states to find
nstates: Int = 10
#: eigensolver  how the lowest states are found: lanczos (the default);
#:     householder_ql or jacobi, from H formed as a matrix (up to
#:     LOWEST_DENSE_MAX basis states); "every dense" (both of those, checked
#:     against each other); or every (all three)
eigensolver = LowestEigenpairs.Lanczos
#: tol  the largest residual norm |H v - E v| a converged state may have;
#:     Lanczos only, ignored with the other methods
tol = 1.0e-8
#: max_iter  the most products H v Lanczos may take; Lanczos only, ignored
#:     with the other methods
max_iter: Int = 2000
#: krylov  the most Lanczos vectors kept at once; the basis restarts from the
#:     lowest Ritz vectors when it is full. Lanczos only, ignored with
#:     the other methods
krylov: Int = 100

using lowest_eigenpairs = eigensolver
settings lanczos(krylov = krylov, tol = tol, max_iter = max_iter)

# ---- the space ----------------------------------------------------------
sps_text: Str = SD_SPS
int_text: Str = USDB_INT
label: Str = "usdb"
match interaction {
    Usdb => {
        sps_text = SD_SPS
        int_text = USDB_INT
        label = "usdb"
    }
    Ckpot => {
        sps_text = P_SPS
        int_text = CKPOT_INT
        label = "ckpot"
    }
}
if len(sps_file) > 0 or len(int_file) > 0 {
    if len(sps_file) == 0 or len(int_file) == 0 {
        stop("sps_file and int_file go together")
    }
    sps_text = read_text(sps_file)
    int_text = read_text(int_file)
    label = "files"
}
space = read_space(sps_text, int_text)
if z < 0 or n < 0 or z > space.ns or n > space.ns {
    stop("z and n must be between 0 and the number of m-states of one species")
}
m2: Int = twice_m
if m2 < 0 {
    m2 = lowest_m2(z, n)
}
if (m2 + z + n) % 2 != 0 {
    stop("twice_m must have the parity of z + n")
}
scale = mass_scale(space, z, n)
same, pn = mscheme_tables(space, scale)

# ---- the basis and the Hamiltonian's pieces -----------------------------
pc = popcounts(space.ns)
protons = make_species(space, pc, z)
neutrons = make_species(space, pc, n)
basis = make_basis(protons, neutrons, m2)
if basis.dim == 0 {
    stop("no Slater determinant has this 2M")
}
hp = species_h(space, pc, same, protons)
hn = species_h(space, pc, same, neutrons)
jp = species_jumps(space, pc, protons)
jn = species_jumps(space, pc, neutrons)

#: counted  y, with one more product counted in products[0]
def counted(y: Arr, products: [Int]) -> Arr {
    products[0] += 1
    return y
}

# ---- the eigensolver ---------------------------------------------------
want: Int = nstates
if want > basis.dim {
    want = basis.dim
}
H = ShellH { b: basis, p: protons, n: neutrons, hp: hp, hn: hn, jp: jp, jn: jn, pn: pn, ns: space.ns }
#: H applied to a vector, counting the products
products: [Int] = [0]
op = fn(x) -> counted(apply_h(H, x), products)
# The lowest states come from the contract lowest_eigenpairs (lib/eigen/lowest),
# by the method `eigensolver` names (the `using` line
# above); Lanczos takes this program's settings (the `settings` line).
energies, psi = lowest_eigenpairs(op, basis.dim, want)
iterations: Int = products[0]
# converged: every state's residual norm |H v - E v| is under tol
converged = true
for k to len(energies) {
    v = zeros(basis.dim)
    for i to basis.dim {
        v[i] = psi[k, i]
    }
    r = apply_h(H, v) - energies[k] * v
    if sqrt(dot(r, r)) > tol {
        converged = false
    }
}
solver_tag: Str = ""
match eigensolver {
    Lanczos => {
        solver_tag = ""
    }
    HouseholderQl => {
        solver_tag = "-householder_ql"
    }
    Jacobi => {
        solver_tag = "-jacobi"
    }
    Every => {
        solver_tag = "-every"
    }
    EveryIterative => {
        solver_tag = "-every_iterative"
    }
    EveryDense => {
        solver_tag = "-every_dense"
    }
}

# ---- what each state is -------------------------------------------------
found: Int = len(energies)
basis_up = make_basis(protons, neutrons, m2 + 2)
spins = zeros(found)
excitation = zeros(found)
occ_p = zeros(found, space.norb)
occ_n = zeros(found, space.norb)
for k to found {
    spins[k] = j_from_j2(j_squared(space, basis, basis_up, protons, neutrons, jp, jn, psi, k))
    excitation[k] = energies[k] - energies[0]
    occ_pk, occ_nk = occupations(space, basis, protons, neutrons, psi, k)
    for a to space.norb {
        occ_p[k, a] = occ_pk[a]
        occ_n[k, a] = occ_nk[a]
    }
}

# ---- results ------------------------------------------------------------
#: ENERGIES  the lowest energies, MeV, relative to the core
ENERGIES = energies
#: J  the angular momentum of each state, from <J^2> = J (J + 1)
J = spins
#: EXCITATION  each energy above the lowest, MeV
EXCITATION = excitation
#: OCC_P  [state, orbit] proton occupation of each orbit, in the .sps order
OCC_P = occ_p
#: OCC_N  [state, orbit] neutron occupation of each orbit
OCC_N = occ_n
#: DIM  the dimension of the M-scheme basis
DIM: Int = basis.dim
#: ITERATIONS  the products H v the eigensolver took
ITERATIONS: Int = iterations
#: CONVERGED  every state's residual norm is under tol
CONVERGED = converged
#: RUN_ID  the run's settings in one string: interaction, z, n, 2M, nstates,
#:     tol, max_iter, krylov, and the eigensolver when it is not Lanczos
RUN_ID: Str = f"shell-{label}-z{z}-n{n}-m2_{m2}-k{want}-tol{tol}-it{max_iter}-kr{krylov}{solver_tag}"

show DIM, ITERATIONS, CONVERGED, RUN_ID
for k to found {
    print(f"{k + 1:3d} {ENERGIES[k]:18.10f} {EXCITATION[k]:14.10f} {J[k]:10.6f}")
}

test "the states are sorted and their spins are whole or half-whole" {
    for k to found {
        if k > 0 {
            assert_true(ENERGIES[k] >= ENERGIES[k - 1])
        }
        twice = 2.0 * J[k]
        assert_near(twice, round(twice), 1.0e-6)
    }
}

test "the occupations add up to z and n" {
    for k to found {
        sp_total = 0.0
        sn_total = 0.0
        for a to space.norb {
            sp_total = sp_total + OCC_P[k, a]
            sn_total = sn_total + OCC_N[k, a]
        }
        assert_near(sp_total, z, 1.0e-10)
        assert_near(sn_total, n, 1.0e-10)
    }
}

modules.name: lib/eigen/lowest
lib/hf/eigen

defs.doc:
read_space  a Space from the text of a .sps ("iso" orbits) and of an
    isospin .int, before any mass scaling
defs.intent: a Space from the text of a .sps ("iso" orbits) and of an isospin .int, before any mass scaling

loops.head: for m2 from -orb_j2[a] to orb_j2[a] + 1 by 2

defs.doc: lowest_m2  the smallest 2M that z + n nucleons can have: 0 or 1
defs.intent: the smallest 2M that z + n nucleons can have: 0 or 1

defs.doc:
mass_scale  the factor (A0 / A)^x of the two-body matrix elements for
    z + n valence nucleons on the core
defs.intent: the factor (A0 / A)^x of the two-body matrix elements for z + n valence nucleons on the core

defs.doc:
mscheme_tables  the antisymmetrized M-scheme matrix elements, scaled by
    `scale`: `same[((al * ns + be) * ns + ga) * ns + de]` for two protons
    or two neutrons (T = 1), and `pn[(al * ns + ga) * ns * ns + be * ns +
    de]` for proton al, ga and neutron be, de (half T = 1 plus half T = 0)
defs.intent: the antisymmetrized M-scheme matrix elements, scaled by `scale`: `same[((al * ns + be) * ns + ga) * ns + de]` for two protons or two neutrons (T = 1), and `pn[(al * ns + ga) * ns * ns + be * ns + de]` for proton al, ga and neutron be, de (half T = 1 plus half T = 0)

defs.doc: popcounts  the number of set bits of every pattern below 2^ns
defs.intent: the number of set bits of every pattern below 2^ns

defs.doc:
make_species  every determinant of n particles in the space, sorted by 2M
    and then by bit pattern, with the occupation of each orbit
defs.intent: every determinant of n particles in the space, sorted by 2M and then by bit pattern, with the occupation of each orbit

defs.doc:
make_basis  the M-scheme basis of total 2M = m2: each proton determinant
    with every neutron determinant of the 2M that completes it
defs.intent: the M-scheme basis of total 2M = m2: each proton determinant with every neutron determinant of the 2M that completes it

defs.doc:
species_h  the one- plus two-body Hamiltonian of one species over its own
    determinants: H = sum e_a n_a + sum over al < be, ga < de of
    V(al be, ga de) a+_al a+_be a_de a_ga, row by row
defs.intent: the one- plus two-body Hamiltonian of one species over its own determinants: H = sum e_a n_a + sum over al < be, ga < de of V(al be, ga de) a+_al a+_be a_de a_ga, row by row

loops.head: for b from a + 1 to ns
for b from a + 1 to ns
for r from poff[key] to poff[key + 1]

defs.doc:
species_jumps  every one-body jump a+_al a_ga of one species (al == ga
    included), sorted by the group of the source determinant and the
    change of 2m: keyoff[g * nd + (dm2 + dmax) / 2] starts each bucket
defs.intent: every one-body jump a+_al a_ga of one species (al == ga included), sorted by the group of the source determinant and the change of 2m: keyoff[g * nd + (dm2 + dmax) / 2] starts each bucket

defs.doc: counted  y, with one more product counted in products[0]
defs.intent: y, with one more product counted in products[0]

defs.doc: apply_h  H x on the pieces H, as a new array
defs.intent: H x on the pieces H, as a new array

defs.doc: j_from_j2  the J whose J (J + 1) is the given expectation value
defs.intent: the J whose J (J + 1) is the given expectation value

defs.doc:
j_squared  <psi| J^2 |psi> = |J+ psi|^2 + M (M + 1), with J+ psi on the
    basis B2 of 2M + 2 (or no basis when 2M is the largest there is)
defs.intent: <psi| J^2 |psi> = |J+ psi|^2 + M (M + 1), with J+ psi on the basis B2 of 2M + 2 (or no basis when 2M is the largest there is)

loops.head: for u from JN.keyoff[key] to JN.keyoff[key + 1]

defs.doc: occupations  the proton and neutron occupation of each orbit in state k
defs.intent: the proton and neutron occupation of each orbit in state k

defs.doc:
data_lines  the lines of a text that carry data: comments after ! or #
    removed, blank lines dropped
defs.intent: the lines of a text that carry data: comments after ! or # removed, blank lines dropped

defs.doc: put_vjt  store one matrix element under all eight orderings it stands for
defs.intent: store one matrix element under all eight orderings it stands for

defs.doc: clebsch  <j1 m1 j2 m2 | J M>, every argument doubled; Racah's formula
defs.intent: <j1 m1 j2 m2 | J M>, every argument doubled; Racah's formula

loops.head: for k from kmin to kmax + 1

defs.doc: vjt_index  where V_JT(ab, cd) sits in Space.vjt
defs.intent: where V_JT(ab, cd) sits in Space.vjt

defs.doc: group_of  the group of determinants with this 2M, or -1 if there is none
defs.intent: the group of determinants with this 2M, or -1 if there is none

defs.doc:
below  how many occupied m-states of pattern s lie below state k: the
    number of transpositions that moves operator k to the front
defs.intent: how many occupied m-states of pattern s lie below state k: the number of transpositions that moves operator k to the front

defs.doc:
apply_h_into  y = H x on the basis B: the proton part on each neutron
    block, the neutron part inside each block, and the proton-neutron part
    as a proton jump times a neutron jump with the opposite change of 2m
defs.intent: y = H x on the basis B: the proton part on each neutron block, the neutron part inside each block, and the proton-neutron part as a proton jump times a neutron jump with the opposite change of 2m

loops.head: for e from HP.off[ip] to HP.off[ip + 1]
for e from HN.off[inn] to HN.off[inn + 1]
for u from JN.keyoff[key] to JN.keyoff[key + 1]

defs.doc:
lanczos  the nev lowest eigenpairs of the operator op by thick-restart
    Lanczos with full reorthogonalization. At `krylov` vectors (at most n)
    the basis restarts from the lowest Ritz vectors, half way between nev
    and krylov. A Ritz pair's residual norm is beta * |last component of
    its eigenvector of T|, tested every LOWEST_CHECK_EVERY steps; the run
    stops when the nev lowest are all under tol, or after max_iter products.
    Returns the values and the Ritz vectors [nev, n]
defs.intent: the nev lowest eigenpairs of the operator op by thick-restart Lanczos with full reorthogonalization. At `krylov` vectors (at most n) the basis restarts from the lowest Ritz vectors, half way between nev and krylov. A Ritz pair's residual norm is beta * |last component of its eigenvector of T|, tested every LOWEST_CHECK_EVERY steps; the run stops when the nev lowest are all under tol, or after max_iter products. Returns the values and the Ritz vectors [nev, n]

loops.head: for k from keep + 1 to kmax + 1

defs.doc:
householder_ql  the nev lowest eigenpairs of op, from its matrix by
    Householder reduction and QL
defs.intent: the nev lowest eigenpairs of op, from its matrix by Householder reduction and QL

defs.doc: jacobi  the nev lowest eigenpairs of op, from its matrix by cyclic Jacobi
defs.intent: the nev lowest eigenpairs of op, from its matrix by cyclic Jacobi

defs.doc:
exchange_phase  the sign of |ba; JT> relative to |ab; JT>,
    (-1)^(ja + jb - J + T)
defs.intent: the sign of |ba; JT> relative to |ab; JT>, (-1)^(ja + jb - J + T)

defs.doc: factorial  n!, as a number
defs.intent: n!, as a number

defs.doc: start_vector  a fixed vector with no symmetry, so it overlaps every state
defs.intent: a fixed vector with no symmetry, so it overlaps every state

defs.doc:
eig_householder_ql  every eigenpair of the symmetric matrix A by
    Householder reduction and implicit QL (lib/hf/eigen), ascending: the
    values, and the vectors as the columns of a matrix
defs.intent: every eigenpair of the symmetric matrix A by Householder reduction and implicit QL (lib/hf/eigen), ascending: the values, and the vectors as the columns of a matrix

defs.doc:
build_matrix  the n by n matrix of the operator op: column i is op
    applied to the i-th unit vector. It holds n^2 numbers, so it stops
    above LOWEST_DENSE_MAX
defs.intent: the n by n matrix of the operator op: column i is op applied to the i-th unit vector. It holds n^2 numbers, so it stops above LOWEST_DENSE_MAX

defs.doc:

defs.doc:
Householder reduction of the symmetric matrix held in `V` to tridiagonal
form (diagonal `d`, subdiagonal `e`), accumulating the transformation in
`V`. JAMA's tred2 with `V` stored transposed: where JAMA reads `V[i, j]`
this reads `V[j, i]`, so its inner loops, which run down a column, walk
along a row of the row-major array. The arithmetic is JAMA's, term for
term; only the storage is transposed.
